## Work with Census profiles

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(cancensus)
```


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

---


Census public use microdata file (PUMF) publishes data at individual level. 

Census Profile publishes data at geographic area level (e.g., whole Canada, province, CMA, CSD, tract).

- The smallest geographic unit for PUMF is CMA.

- Use PUMF if the unit of your analysis is individuals. Use Profile if it is geographic areas.

To see the type of available information at a geographic level, go to the '[Census Profile, 2021 Census](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/dp-pd/prof/index.cfm?Lang=E)' page at the Statistics Canada website (Google it). Click 'Canada' in the Browse box. 


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.dim=c(9,9)}
csd <- get_census(dataset = "CA21", regions = list(CMA = "59933"), level = "CSD", use_cache = TRUE, geo_format = "sf")
ggplot(csd) +
  geom_sf() +
  geom_sf_text(aes(label = name |> str_extract(".*(?=\\(..\\))")), data = csd |> filter(name |> str_detect("(CY)|(DM)|(IM)")), size = 5) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "CSD (Census Subdivision) boundaries") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

---


```{r echo=FALSE, fig.dim=c(9,9)}
ct <- get_census(dataset = "CA21", regions = list(CMA = "59933"), level = "CT", use_cache = TRUE, geo_format = "sf")
ggplot(ct) +
  geom_sf() +
  ggtitle("Census tract boundaries") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```

We will learn how to import Census profile data into R, using `cancensus` package. For example, 


::: {.scroll-output}

::: {.tiny}
```{r echo=FALSE}
get_census("CA21", list(C = "01"), level = "CMA", vectors = "v_CA21_4311") |>
  arrange(desc(Population)) |>
  select(matches("GeoUID|Name|^v_")) |>
  filter(!is.na(`v_CA21_4311: Median value of dwellings ($) (60)`)) |>
  kable()
```
:::
:::

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.

---



::: {.small}
It is difficult to interpret data at small geographic units. We will learn how to show them on a map.
:::

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.dim=c(9,9), fig.align='center'}
get_census("CA21", list(CMA = "59933"), level = "CT", vectors = "v_CA21_4311", geo_format = "sf") |>
  select(matches("GeoUID|^v_")) |>
  filter(!is.na(`v_CA21_4311: Median value of dwellings ($) (60)`)) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = `v_CA21_4311: Median value of dwellings ($) (60)`)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Median dwelling value\n (Census Tract)", labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 0.000001, suffix = "M")) +
  theme_void()
```


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("cancensus")

```

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(cancensus)
library(tidyverse)
```

[Sources]

---


Click [here](https://censusmapper.ca/users/sign_up) to sign up for Censusmapper.ca to obtain your own API key. You can use your Google, Facebook or Twitter account.

Run the following code <i>in Console just once</i>, to store your API key in your computer and automatically use it in API calls. 
```{r eval=FALSE}
set_cancensus_api_key("your_api_key", install = TRUE)
```

Run the following code <i>in Console just once</i>, to set the cache folder.
```{r eval=FALSE}
set_cancensus_cache_path("~/cancensus_cache", install = TRUE)
```


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

---


Suppose we want to calculate Chinese shares by CMA.

```{r}
chinese_cma <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21", regions = list(C = "01"),
  vectors = c("v_CA21_4872", "v_CA21_4881"), level = "CMA"
)
```

This code downloads total population and the number of Chinese by CMA.

The following columns are included by default: Area (sq km), Population, Dwellings, Households.


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

---



::: {.scroll-output}

::: {.tiny}
```{r echo=FALSE}
chinese_cma |> kable()
```
:::
:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

---



::: {.tiny}
```{r eval=FALSE}
chinese_cma |>
  transmute(
    `Region Name`,
    Chinese_share = `v_CA21_4881: Chinese` / `v_CA21_4872: Total - Visible minority for the population in private households`
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Chinese_share))
```
:::

::: {.scroll-output}

::: {.tiny}
```{r echo=FALSE}
chinese_cma |>
  transmute(`Region Name`, Chinese_share = `v_CA21_4881: Chinese` / `v_CA21_4872: Total - Visible minority for the population in private households`) |>
  arrange(desc(Chinese_share)) |>
  kable()
```
:::
:::

[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.

## vectors= c("v_CA21_4872","v_CA21_4881")

At [the Canada page of Census Profile, 2021 Census website](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/dp-pd/prof/details/page.cfm?Lang=E&Geo1=PR&Code1=01&Geo2=&Code2=&SearchText=Canada&SearchType=Begins&SearchPR=01&B1=All&TABID=1&type=0), find the characteric label you are looking for.

Note the hierarchy of the characteristics. Chinese < Total visible minority population < Total - Visible minority for the population in private households - 25% sample data

```{r eval=FALSE}
explore_census_vectors("CA21")
```

Type "Chinese" in the Search box.


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

## Map {.c407-dense}

```{r}
chinese_csd_van_sf <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",
  regions = list(CMA = "59933"),
  vectors = c("v_CA21_4872", "v_CA21_4881"),
  level = "CSD",
  geo_format = "sf"
)
```

geo_format = 'sf' create an sf object, which extends data.frame-like objects with the geometry column.


```{r}
class(chinese_csd_van_sf)
```


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

---



::: {.scroll-output}

```{r echo=FALSE}
chinese_csd_van_sf |> kable()
```

:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/16_census_profile.Rmd`.
:::

::: {.tiny}
```{r}

  transmute(
    `Region Name`,
    Chinese_share = `v_CA21_4881: Chinese` / `v_CA21_4872: Total - Visible minority for the population in private households`
```
